title: Teams That Perform Acts of Community Service
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that community service activities are among the most powerful teambuilding tools available, more effective than typical corporate offsites because they strip away the everyday competitive dynamics of work. The author emphasizes that full team participation is essential — no sidelines allowed — for the unifying effect to take hold, and offers an extensive, creative list of service options beyond the standard Habitat for Humanity or food-bank fare. The underlying claim is that the real value isn't the community impact itself but the camaraderie, communication, and coordination skills teams build in the process.
points: Community service activities build team unity more effectively than typical teambuilding exercises because they remove the pretense of everyday work competition.
Full participation is essential — the model breaks down if any team members opt out or sit on the sidelines.
The author offers a long, unconventional list of service ideas well beyond the usual Habitat for Humanity or food bank options (vaccination drives, community gardens, public art, bike building).
The real payoff of service activities is less the community impact itself and more the camaraderie and communication skills teams build while collaborating on something outside normal work.
quotes: Of the many teambuilding activities available to organizations, perhaps none is as powerful as team members performing a community service together.
Because it involves helping others and does not focus on the everyday work of the organization, team members drop any pretense and build camaraderie.
The key to such activities is to find a project everyone on the team wants to contribute to. Everyone must engage. No one can sit on the sidelines or choose not to contribute.

Consider this shortlist of activities: Vaccination drives and sponsoring health fairs, fostering animals awaiting adoption, disaster preparation, creating community gardens, revitalizing local parks, planting trees
Leaders who facilitate acts of service build teams in the process. When team members use their talents to serve the community, they lift themselves up and learn how to better collaborate.
